overview: Major Current Events: 189 official Qs (2008-2025). International 89, National 75, Andhra Pradesh 25. Mostly one-liners (173). From 2024 APPSC shifted to statement-based, multiple-correct, matching and odd-pair formats. Asked: who won or holds what, where an event was held, the year's theme, the date of a Day, and an AP institution or GI. Most items date from the 12-18 months before the exam.

possibility.angle: International awards and prizes (Nobel, Oscar, Ondaatje, Fields, Gandhi-named awards)
possibility.what_they_ask: Laureate for a category and year, the field or theme of the prize-winning work, the laureate's country

possibility.angle: Summits, organisations, membership and heads (SAARC, CHOGM, G-8/G20, EU, BRICS, UN, WHO, IMF)
possibility.evidence: about 20 Qs: summits/membership 10 (2008×4, 2012×2, 2017×2, 2019, 2024) + heads of bodies and States 10 (2008-2024)
possibility.what_they_ask: Venue and dates of an edition, member count or new members, periodicity, current Secretary-General / DG / MD / CEO, newly elected presidents

possibility.angle: International places, conflicts and policy events in news (Doklam, Aleppo, Brexit, Greek referendum, Venezuela demonetisation, Indus Treaty, power trade)
possibility.evidence: about 30 Qs spread over all six years (2008-2024)
possibility.what_they_ask: Country of a place, the two parties to a deal or dispute, what a referendum or law was about, who brokered a treaty

possibility.angle: Days and annual themes (UN days, WEF/IWD/Human Rights Day/Education Day themes, Civil Services and PSB Day)
possibility.what_they_ask: Exact date of a Day; the theme for the asked year (distractors are other years' themes)

possibility.angle: Sports results (World Cups, Olympics, Grand Slams, IPL, leagues, Indian players' titles and deals)
possibility.what_they_ask: Champion (not runner-up), host city, medal table order, the player's partner or event, an endorsement brand

possibility.angle: Global indices and reports (CPI, LPI, NTI index, India Skills Report)
possibility.what_they_ask: India's rank in the latest edition, what the index measures, who tops it, State findings

possibility.angle: National appointments and institutions (CEC, service chiefs, Law Commission, LG, scientific adviser, committees)
possibility.what_they_ask: Name of the new holder of a post; which body did an act (Law Commission vs ministry)

possibility.angle: Defence inductions and exercises (INS ships and subs, Hawk AJT, Rafale, MILAN)
possibility.what_they_ask: Where commissioned or held, which command, the maker, the vessel type

possibility.angle: National awards and honours (Padma, Arjuna, Magsaysay to Indians, Sahitya Akademi, BWF, peace prizes)
possibility.what_they_ask: Award to a person with the correct field or discipline; the reason for the award; jury chair

possibility.angle: National schemes, economy and governance news (UJALA, EPF rate, demonetisation, SEBI T+0, Economic Survey ideas, RIIN, BARC)
possibility.evidence: about 30 Qs in National 'misc' news across 2008-2025
possibility.what_they_ask: Aim of a scheme, a rate or figure for a year, the State behind a register or initiative, the agency that measures something

possibility.angle: Science congresses and sessions (ISC, IHC, Seed Congress, book fair themes)
possibility.what_they_ask: Venue of the nth session; theme of the year's event
Section number for a subject; how assets and balances are divided; how delimitation can happen
Which product is or is not a registered GI as of a cut-off date

possibility.angle: AP institutions, firsts, investments and awards (Urdu University, OCTOPUS, Justice City, HRIDAY, smoke-free State, EV plant, e-gov award, Telugu Sahitya Akademi)
possibility.what_they_ask: City or district of an institution or investment, year a force or body was set up, project that won an award, date of a State declaration

traps.trap: [Wrong year] Another year's theme or edition used as a distractor
traps.spot: Theme or venue questions whose options all sound right
traps.fix: Store themes as year → theme ladders. Adjacent years' themes are the usual lures.
traps.pyq: Human Rights Day 2016 → 'Stand up for someone's rights today' ('Our Rights, Our Freedoms, Always' was 2015) [prelims-2017#133]; Education Day 2024 → 'Learning for lasting peace' [prelims-2024#97]

traps.trap: Runner-up or the other finalist offered as winner
traps.spot: Both finalists appear in the options
traps.fix: Recall the final as 'X beat Y'.
traps.pyq: Wimbledon 2008 → Venus beat Serena [group2-2008-paper1#46]; World Series Hockey 2012 → Sher-e-Punjab beat Pune Strykers [group2-2012-paper1#126]

traps.trap: Ranking by gold vs by total medals
traps.spot: 'Arrange in descending order of total medals'
traps.fix: Rio 2016 totals: USA 121, China 70, GB 67, Russia 56. By golds, GB (27) was ahead of China (26).
traps.pyq: Total medals → USA, China, Great Britain, Russia [prelims-2017#80]

traps.spot: Two options sharing a surname or a first name
traps.fix: Check the full name. Anil Baijal (LG Delhi), not Pradip Baijal. Yashwant Sinha, not Yashwant Singh. V.R.S. Natarajan, not N. Natarajan.
traps.pyq: New LG of Delhi → Anil Baijal [prelims-2017#21]; BEML chief suspended → V.R.S. Natarajan [group2-2012-paper1#8]

traps.spot: 'Present', 'new' or 'newly elected' with a former holder in the options
traps.fix: Read the post as of the exam date: the 2017 paper meant Lagarde (IMF) and Guterres (UN). In 2024 a former Guatemalan president (Pérez Molina, 2012-15) was paired as 'newly elected'; Arévalo took office in Jan 2024.
traps.pyq: IMF MD (2017 exam) → Christine Lagarde [prelims-2017#5]; 'Fernando Pérez Molina : Guatemala' is an odd pair [prelims-2024#119]

traps.trap: One swapped detail inside a long statement (venue, command, person)
traps.fix: Check venue, organiser and person separately. MILAN = Eastern Naval Command, Visakhapatnam. Asian Winter Games 2025 = Harbin. Indira Gandhi Prize 2023 jury chair = Shivshankar Menon.
traps.pyq: 'Southern Naval Command' makes MILAN statement I false [prelims-2024#100]; 'held at Beijing' is false → II and IV [prelims-2024#91]; 'chaired by R.M. Lodha' is false [prelims-2024#115]

traps.trap: Right person, wrong category or field
traps.spot: Padma, Sahitya Akademi or FIH/ICC award lists
traps.fix: Check the field column (Art vs Literature vs Social Work) and the sub-award (main, Bal or Yuva).
traps.pyq: Padma Shri 2024 Art → Drona Bhuyan, Ghulam Nabi Dar, Dasari Kondappa (Rajaram Jain is Literature) [prelims-2024#93]; Patanjali Sastri won for short stories, not poetry [prelims-2024#112]

traps.trap: GI status checked against the wrong cut-off date
traps.spot: 'Not registered as GI as per details till …'
traps.fix: Bandar (Machilipatnam) Laddu was registered only in 2017. Tirupati Laddu and Uppada Jamdani were registered in 2009, and Guntur Sannam chilli in 2011.
traps.pyq: Not GI till Nov 2016 → Bandaru Laddu [prelims-2017#115]

traps.trap: Town attached to the wrong scheme
traps.spot: AP towns in HRIDAY / PRASAD / Smart City options
traps.fix: HRIDAY = heritage cities. Amaravati (Buddhist heritage) is AP's HRIDAY town. Pilgrim towns go under PRASAD.

traps.trap: Neighbouring section numbers of the AP Reorganisation Act
traps.spot: Options are four consecutive section numbers
traps.fix: Anchor Part VII (assets and liabilities, Secs 47-67): Sec 53 = PSU assets. Cash balances are adjusted in RBI books on the population ratio.

techniques.name: [Edition arithmetic] Session number to year
techniques.how: For annual events, year = known year ± (session gap). The ISC meets each January: 100th Kolkata 2013, 104th Tirupati 2017.
techniques.example: 104th ISC → Tirupati, 2017 [prelims-2017#144]; 95th = 9 sessions earlier = Jan 2008 → Visakhapatnam [group2-2008-paper1#50]

techniques.name: Strike-by-surest-item in multiple-correct sets
techniques.how: Pick the item you know is out (or in). Drop every option containing (or lacking) it, then repeat with the next.
techniques.example: BRICS from 1 Jan 2024: Argentina declined, so drop options with II. Indonesia joined only in 2025, so drop I, III, V → I, IV and V [prelims-2024#110]

techniques.name: Lock unique pairs in matching
techniques.how: Fix the one or two pairs you are sure of. Usually the remaining option set collapses before you need the hard ones.
techniques.example: Sheetal Devi = para-archery (b-IV) drops option 2; Diksha Dagar = golf (d-I) drops option 3; Ritu Negi = kabaddi (a-II) drops option 1 → a-II, b-IV, c-V, d-I, e-III [prelims-2024#95]

techniques.name: Institutional logic elimination
techniques.how: Use how institutions work. Embassies sit in capitals and consulates elsewhere. Parliamentary committees are chaired by MPs, not ministers. Bills are 'passed' by a House.
techniques.example: Israel's new consulate: Delhi already has the embassy → Bengaluru [group2-2012-paper1#100]; Finance Standing Committee chair → Yashwant Sinha, not FM Pranab Mukherjee [group2-2012-paper1#6]

techniques.name: Name-clue decoding
techniques.how: Titles and mission names often encode the answer: a translated name, a number with meaning, or an initialism.
techniques.example: 'Half-Lion' = Narasimha → P.V. Narasimha Rao [prelims-2017#7]; 'Mission XI Million' = a football eleven before the U-17 World Cup [mains-2017-paper1#17]

techniques.name: Arithmetic and plausibility check
techniques.how: When a number is embedded in the stem, test whether it fits a known cycle or total before guessing.
techniques.example: 'after 221 years' = 13 × 17 → periodical cicada broods co-emerging → Double Cicada Explosion [prelims-2024#116]

techniques.name: Convention anchors for heads of bodies
techniques.how: Use the title and convention. IMF head = Managing Director (European by convention). World Bank = President (American). UNSG terms start 1 January.
techniques.example: Ban Ki-moon took over → 1 January 2007 (drops the July options) [group2-2008-paper1#62]; IMF MD in 2017 → Lagarde [prelims-2017#5]

checklist: Time-stamp the question: which year is 'present', 'new' or 'recent' for this exam paper?
Is the stem asking winner or runner-up, first or second, gold or total, Indian first or world first?
For a theme or venue, recall the asked year and the years on either side, since those are the lures
Check full names and initials when two options look alike
Statement sets: test venue, organiser and person one at a time; strike options as soon as one statement fails
Use institutional logic (capital = embassy, MPs chair committees, a House passes bills) to drop impossible options
AP items: tie the institution or investment to its city or district and the GI to its registration year
